claim: VG3-Cre mice were crossed to a novel transgenic strain (Ai148) expressing the genetically encoded Ca2+ indicator GCaMP6f in a Cre-dependent manner enhanced by tTA-based transcriptional amplification.
source: We crossed VG3-Cre mice to a novel transgenic strain (Ai148) expressing the genetically encoded Ca2+ indicator GCaMP6f in a Cre-dependent manner enhanced by tTA-based transcriptional amplification.
evidence: This is a methodological statement describing the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: GCaMP6f labeling in VG3-Cre:Ai148 retinas was mostly restricted to VG3-ACs with sparse off-target expression in RGCs.
source: Staining for VGluT3 confirmed that GCaMP6f labeling in VG3-Cre:Ai148 retinas was mostly restricted to VG3-ACs (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) with sparse off-target expression in RGCs (Grimes et al., 2011; Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and cited references.

claim: Contrast preferences (ON vs. OFF) varied across VG3-AC arbors depending on the laminar position of neurites.
source: Contrast preferences (ON vs. OFF) varied across VG3-AC arbors depending on the laminar position of neurites, with ON responses preferring larger stimuli than OFF responses.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by imaging data presented in Figure 1.

claim: ON responses prefer larger stimuli than OFF responses in VG3-AC neurites.
source: Contrast preferences (ON vs. OFF) varied across VG3-AC arbors depending on the laminar position of neurites, with ON responses preferring larger stimuli than OFF responses.
evidence: This finding is supported by experimental data on stimulus size preferences shown in Figure 2.

claim: Imaging population activity revealed continuous topographic maps of visual space in the VG3-AC plexus.
source: Although arbors of neighboring cells overlap extensively, imaging population activity revealed continuous topographic maps of visual space in the VG3-AC plexus.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by imaging data and analysis presented in Figure 3.

claim: All VG3-AC neurites responded strongly to object motion.
source: All VG3-AC neurites responded strongly to object motion, but remained silent during global image motion.
evidence: This finding is supported by experimental data from motion stimuli presented in Figure 4.

claim: VG3-AC neurites remained silent during global image motion.
source: All VG3-AC neurites responded strongly to object motion, but remained silent during global image motion.
evidence: This finding is supported by experimental data from motion stimuli presented in Figure 4.

claim: VG3-AC arbors limit vertical integration of contrast information.
source: Thus, VG3-AC arbors limit vertical and lateral integration of contrast and location information, respectively.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the depth-dependent contrast preferences observed in the data.

claim: VG3-AC arbors limit lateral integration of location information.
source: Thus, VG3-AC arbors limit vertical and lateral integration of contrast and location information, respectively.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the topographic mapping data showing local processing.

claim: Local processing enables the dense VG3-AC plexus to contribute precise object motion signals to diverse targets without distorting target-specific contrast preferences and spatial receptive fields.
source: We propose that this local processing enables the dense VG3-AC plexus to contribute precise object motion signals to diverse targets without distorting target-specific contrast preferences and spatial receptive fields.
evidence: This is a proposed interpretation of the experimental findings regarding the functional significance of local processing.

claim: Neurons receive most of their synaptic input on large intricately branched dendritic arborizations.
source: Neurons receive most of their synaptic input on large intricately branched dendritic arborizations.
evidence: This is a statement of established neuroscience knowledge.

claim: Distributed inputs were traditionally thought to be summed linearly at the cell body.
source: Traditionally, distributed inputs were thought to be summed linearly at the cell body (Yuste, 2011).
evidence: This is a historical perspective supported by citation.

claim: Recent studies uncovered extensive local processing and clustered plasticity of synaptic inputs, which enhance the computational power of dendrites.
source: However, recent studies uncovered extensive local processing and clustered plasticity of synaptic inputs, which enhance the computational power of dendrites (Grienberger et al., 2015; Harvey and Svoboda, 2007; Kleindienst et al., 2011; London and Häusser, 2005; Losonczy et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Local processing occurs in terminal axon arbors, in which presynaptic inhibition and inhomogeneous distributions of voltage-gated ion channels can diversify the output of a single neuron.
source: Although less studied, similar local processing occurs in terminal axon arbors, in which presynaptic inhibition and inhomogeneous distributions of voltage-gated ion channels can diversify the output of a single neuron (Debanne, 2004; Asari and Meister, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Amacrine cells are a diverse class of interneurons in the retina.
source: Amacrine cells (ACs) are a diverse class of interneurons in the retina (Helmstaedter et al., 2013; MacNeil and Masland, 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Most of the approximately 50 AC types lack separate dendrites and axons and receive input and provide output through the same neurites.
source: Most of the approximately 50 AC types lack separate dendrites and axons and receive input and provide output through the same neurites (Diamond, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about amacrine cell anatomy supported by citation.

claim: Starburst ACs are critical for direction selectivity.
source: Among the few AC types that have been studied in detail, starburst and A17 ACs are critical for direction selectivity and dim light signaling, respectively (Grimes et al., 2015; Amthor et al., 2002; Vlasits et al., 2014; Yonehara et al., 2016; Yoshida et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: A17 ACs are critical for dim light signaling.
source: Among the few AC types that have been studied in detail, starburst and A17 ACs are critical for direction selectivity and dim light signaling, respectively (Grimes et al., 2015; Amthor et al., 2002; Vlasits et al., 2014; Yonehara et al., 2016; Yoshida et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: The radially symmetric arbors of starburst ACs receive synaptic input and release neurotransmitters near and far from the soma, respectively.
source: The radially symmetric arbors of starburst ACs receive synaptic input and release neurotransmitters near and far from the soma, respectively (Ding et al., 2016; Vlasits et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Euler et al. (2002) discovered by two-photon Ca2+ imaging that the four to six primary neurites of starburst ACs with their daughter branches function as independent centrifugal motion sensors.
source: In a seminal study, Euler et al. (2002) discovered by two-photon Ca2+ imaging that the four to six primary neurites of starburst ACs with their daughter branches function as independent centrifugal motion sensors.
evidence: This is a description of a previous finding supported by citation.

claim: A17 ACs were shown to process converging inputs from rod bipolar cells separately.
source: Similarly, A17 ACs were shown to process converging inputs from rod bipolar cells separately (Grimes et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: For most AC types, whether arbors process inputs locally or integrate them globally and what specific stimulus features neurites encode remains unknown.
source: For most AC types, however, whether arbors process inputs locally or integrate them globally and what specific stimulus features neurites encode remains unknown.
evidence: This identifies a gap in current knowledge that motivates the study.

claim: Synaptic communication in the retina occurs in dense neuropils in which arbors of neighboring cells overlap extensively.
source: As in most parts of the nervous system, synaptic communication in the retina occurs in dense neuropils in which arbors of neighboring cells overlap extensively (Helmstaedter et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Population coding in sensory and motor systems has been studied at the level of cell bodies.
source: Population coding in sensory and motor systems has been studied at the level of cell bodies (Arnson and Holy, 2013; Churchland et al., 2012; Leonardo and Meister, 2013), but how cell-type-specific information is organized in population activity in neuropils has not been explored.
evidence: This describes the state of the field supported by citations.

claim: How cell-type-specific information is organized in population activity in neuropils has not been explored.
source: Population coding in sensory and motor systems has been studied at the level of cell bodies (Arnson and Holy, 2013; Churchland et al., 2012; Leonardo and Meister, 2013), but how cell-type-specific information is organized in population activity in neuropils has not been explored.
evidence: This identifies a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: VG3-AC neurites stratify broadly in the center of the inner plexiform layer (IPL) forming a dense plexus in which processes of approximately seven cells overlap at any point.
source: VG3-AC neurites stratify broadly in the center of the inner plexiform layer (IPL) forming a dense plexus in which processes of approximately seven cells overlap at any point (Haverkamp and Wässle, 2004; Johnson et al., 2004; Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This anatomical description is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In somatic patch clamp recordings, VG3-ACs depolarize to light increments (ON) and decrements (OFF) restricted to their receptive field center.
source: In somatic patch clamp recordings, VG3-ACs depolarize to light increments (ON) and decrements (OFF) restricted to their receptive field center, but hyperpolarize to large ON and OFF stimuli that include their receptive field surround (Kim et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2014; Grimes et al., 2011).
evidence: This physiological property is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: VG3-ACs hyperpolarize to large ON and OFF stimuli that include their receptive field surround.
source: In somatic patch clamp recordings, VG3-ACs depolarize to light increments (ON) and decrements (OFF) restricted to their receptive field center, but hyperpolarize to large ON and OFF stimuli that include their receptive field surround (Kim et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2014; Grimes et al., 2011).
evidence: This physiological property is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: VG3-ACs depolarize strongly to local object motion but hyperpolarize during global image motion as occurs during eye movements.
source: In addition, VG3-ACs depolarize strongly to local object motion but hyperpolarize during global image motion as occurs during eye movements (Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This physiological property is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: VG3-ACs are dual transmitter neurons.
source: VG3-ACs are dual transmitter neurons.
evidence: This is established knowledge about VG3-ACs.

claim: VG3-ACs provide glutamatergic input to a group of motion-sensitive retinal ganglion cell (RGC) types with diverse contrast and stimulus-size preferences.
source: They provide glutamatergic input to a group of motion-sensitive retinal ganglion cell (RGC) types with diverse contrast and stimulus-size preferences (Krishnaswamy et al., 2015; Kim et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2014), and provide glycinergic input to Suppressed-by-Contrast RGCs (SbC-RGCs), inhibiting selectively responses to small OFF stimuli (Lee et al., 2016; Tien et al., 2016; Tien et al., 2015).
evidence: This circuit connectivity is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: VG3-ACs provide glycinergic input to Suppressed-by-Contrast RGCs (SbC-RGCs), inhibiting selectively responses to small OFF stimuli.
source: They provide glutamatergic input to a group of motion-sensitive retinal ganglion cell (RGC) types with diverse contrast and stimulus-size preferences (Krishnaswamy et al., 2015; Kim et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2014), and provide glycinergic input to Suppressed-by-Contrast RGCs (SbC-RGCs), inhibiting selectively responses to small OFF stimuli (Lee et al., 2016; Tien et al., 2016; Tien et al., 2015).
evidence: This circuit connectivity is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Images were acquired at 9.5 Hz with a pixel density of 4.7 pixels / μm2.
source: We imaged GCaMP6f signals in scan fields (33 × 33 μm for Figures 1, 2 and 4; 13 × 100 μm for Figure 3) in the IPL of flat-mounted retinas at 9.5 Hz with a pixel density of 4.7 pixels / μm2.
evidence: This is a methodological detail of the experimental approach.

claim: Recording depths of scan fields were registered by their relative distance to the outer and inner boundaries of the IPL (0–100%).
source: Recording depths of scan fields were registered by their relative distance to the outer and inner boundaries of the IPL (0–100%) detected by imaging transmitted laser light (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes the method for determining imaging depth.

claim: Visual stimulation (385 nm) was spectrally separated from GCaMP6f imaging (excitation: 940 nm, peak emission: 515 nm).
source: Visual stimulation (385 nm) was spectrally separated from GCaMP6f imaging (excitation: 940 nm, peak emission: 515 nm); and recordings were obtained from the ventral retina, where S-opsin dominates (Haverkamp et al., 2005; Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the experimental setup.

claim: Recordings were obtained from the ventral retina, where S-opsin dominates.
source: Visual stimulation (385 nm) was spectrally separated from GCaMP6f imaging (excitation: 940 nm, peak emission: 515 nm); and recordings were obtained from the ventral retina, where S-opsin dominates (Haverkamp et al., 2005; Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This methodological choice is supported by citations about opsin distribution.

claim: Polarity indices differed between IPL depths (p<10−16, Kruskal-Wallis one-way ANOVA).
source: Polarity indices differed between IPL depths (p<10−16, Kruskal-Wallis one-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis.

claim: ROIs at 21% and 29% IPL depth were more biased to OFF responses than at other depths (p<10−4 compared to 37%; p<10−7 for 44–60%).
source: ROIs at 21% and 29% IPL depth were more biased to OFF responses than at other depths (p<10−4 compared to 37%; p<10−7 for 44–60%).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis.

claim: ROIs from 51–60% IPL depth were more biased to ON than ROIs from 21–44% (p<10−7).
source: ROIs from 51–60% IPL depth were more biased to ON than ROIs from 21–44% (p<10−7).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the data analysis.

claim: The ratio of ON and OFF signals across VG3-AC arbors closely followed stratification patterns of ON and OFF bipolar cell axons in the IPL.
source: The ratio of ON and OFF signals across VG3-AC arbors closely followed stratification patterns of ON and OFF bipolar cell axons in the IPL (Figure 1E) (Helmstaedter et al., 2013; Franke et al., 2017; Greene et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an observation from the data supported by comparison to cited literature.

claim: Response polarities of VG3-AC neurites were less extreme than those reported for bipolar cell axons.
source: However, response polarities of VG3-AC neurites were less extreme than those reported for bipolar cell axons (Borghuis et al., 2013; Franke et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous findings supported by citations.

claim: Local bipolar cell innervation patterns and restricted postsynaptic signal (voltage and/or Ca2+) spread determine contrast preferences of VG3-AC neurites.
source: This suggests that local bipolar cell innervation patterns and restricted postsynaptic signal (voltage and/or Ca2+) spread determine contrast preferences of VG3-AC neurites and limit vertical integration of visual information in their arbors.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: ON receptive field centers of VG3-AC neurites were consistently larger than OFF receptive field centers, independent of IPL depth.
source: ON receptive field centers of VG3-AC neurites were consistently larger than OFF receptive field centers, independent of IPL depth (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: At all depths, only small stimuli (diameter <400 μm) elicited Ca2+ transients in VG3-AC neurites.
source: At all depths, only small stimuli (diameter <400 μm) elicited Ca2+ transients in VG3-AC neurites (Figure 2A and Video 1) and size-selectivity indices of ROIs were uniformly high (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), indicating that receptive field surrounds are strong across VG3-AC arbors.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data.

claim: Size-selectivity indices of ROIs were uniformly high, indicating that receptive field surrounds are strong across VG3-AC arbors.
source: At all depths, only small stimuli (diameter <400 μm) elicited Ca2+ transients in VG3-AC neurites (Figure 2A and Video 1) and size-selectivity indices of ROIs were uniformly high (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), indicating that receptive field surrounds are strong across VG3-AC arbors.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the size-selectivity data.

claim: Larger dendritic territories of the ON compared to the OFF bipolar cells that provide input to VG3-ACs could explain why ON receptive field centers are larger than OFF receptive field centers.
source: This could be due to larger dendritic territories of the ON compared to the OFF bipolar cells that provide input to VG3-ACs (Behrens et al., 2016), and/or the fact that ON but not OFF bipolar cell axons are gap junctionally coupled to AII ACs (Marc et al., 2014; Demb and Singer, 2015; Bloomfield and Völgyi, 2009).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: ON but not OFF bipolar cell axons are gap junctionally coupled to AII ACs.
source: This could be due to larger dendritic territories of the ON compared to the OFF bipolar cells that provide input to VG3-ACs (Behrens et al., 2016), and/or the fact that ON but not OFF bipolar cell axons are gap junctionally coupled to AII ACs (Marc et al., 2014; Demb and Singer, 2015; Bloomfield and Völgyi, 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: ON and OFF receptive field centers were smaller than VG3-AC arbors and only slightly larger than bipolar cell receptive field centers.
source: Both ON and OFF receptive field centers were smaller than VG3-AC arbors and only slightly larger than bipolar cell receptive field centers (Franke et al., 2017; Schwartz et al., 2012; Purgert and Lukasiewicz, 2015), supporting the notion that local input from a small number of bipolar cells shapes spatial receptive fields of VG3-AC neurites with limited lateral integration of visual information in their arbors.
evidence: This is a comparison to previous findings supported by citations.

claim: Local input from a small number of bipolar cells shapes spatial receptive fields of VG3-AC neurites with limited lateral integration of visual information in their arbors.
source: Both ON and OFF receptive field centers were smaller than VG3-AC arbors and only slightly larger than bipolar cell receptive field centers (Franke et al., 2017; Schwartz et al., 2012; Purgert and Lukasiewicz, 2015), supporting the notion that local input from a small number of bipolar cells shapes spatial receptive fields of VG3-AC neurites with limited lateral integration of visual information in their arbors.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the receptive field size data.

claim: ON and OFF responses were equally transient across VG3-AC arbors.
source: In contrast to differences in their spatial tuning, ON and OFF responses were equally transient across VG3-AC arbors (Figure 2A,D,E).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Measurements of response transience were not limited by the image acquisition rate.
source: By increasing our scan rate from 9.5 Hz to 37.9 Hz, we confirmed that our measurements of response transience were not limited by the image acquisition rate (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a control experiment validating the measurement approach.

claim: Even for single pixels, the accuracy with which naive Bayes classifiers could assign neurite activity to specific parts of the topographic map based on receptive field positions was remarkably high.
source: Even for single pixels, this accuracy was remarkably high (Figure 3E,F,H); and the minimal distance at which different regions of the map could be distinguished with >75% accuracy (i.e. minimal separable distance) decreased further when considering that multiple pixels represent the activity of VG3-AC neurite processing domains (median number of pixels per ROI: 10, Figure 3G,I).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of topographic mapping data.

claim: The minimal separable distance decreased when considering that multiple pixels represent the activity of VG3-AC neurite processing domains.
source: Even for single pixels, this accuracy was remarkably high (Figure 3E,F,H); and the minimal distance at which different regions of the map could be distinguished with >75% accuracy (i.e. minimal separable distance) decreased further when considering that multiple pixels represent the activity of VG3-AC neurite processing domains (median number of pixels per ROI: 10, Figure 3G,I).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of topographic mapping data.

claim: Local processing generates precise topographic maps of visual space in the population activity of the dense VG3-AC plexus.
source: Thus, local processing generates precise topographic maps of visual space in the population activity of the dense VG3-AC plexus.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the topographic mapping data.

claim: At all IPL depths, isolated motion of the center grating elicited robust Ca2+ transients in VG3-AC neurites, which remained silent during simultaneous motion of gratings in center and surround (i.e. global motion).
source: At all IPL depths, isolated motion of the center grating elicited robust Ca2+ transients in VG3-AC neurites, which remained silent during simultaneous motion of gratings in center and surround (i.e. global motion) (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and Video 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the motion stimulus experiments.

claim: Local motion preference indices of >70% of ROIs were >0.8.
source: As a result, local motion preference indices (see Materials and methods) of >70% of ROIs were >0.8 (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the motion stimulus data.

claim: VG3-AC neurites exhibit uniform object motion sensitivity in spite of the diversity of responses to contrast steps.
source: Thus, in spite of the diversity of responses to contrast steps, VG3-AC neurites exhibit uniform object motion sensitivity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the motion sensitivity data.

claim: If VG3-ACs integrated visual information globally, excitatory receptive fields of W3-RGCs would expand considerably, lowering the precision with which the position of moving objects could be inferred from their activity.
source: If VG3-ACs integrated visual information globally, excitatory receptive fields of W3-RGCs would expand considerably, lowering the precision with which the position of moving objects could be inferred from their activity (Jacoby and Schwartz, 2017).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the functional consequences of global integration.

claim: Input from VG3-ACs is required for normal object-motion-sensitive responses of W3-RGCs.
source: Input from VG3-ACs is required for normal object-motion-sensitive responses of W3-RGCs (Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous research supported by citation.

claim: W3-RGCs detect movements in a small area of visual space closely aligned with their dendrites.
source: VG3-ACs provide glutamatergic input to W3-RGCs, which detect movements in a small area of visual space closely aligned with their dendrites (Kim et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous research supported by citations.

claim: The depth-dependent shift in contrast preferences across neurite arbors likely enables VG3-ACs to contribute motion-sensitive excitatory input to ON DSGCs, ON-OFF DSGCs, and OFFα-RGCs without altering the diverse contrast preference of these targets.
source: The depth-dependent shift in contrast preferences across neurite arbors likely enables VG3-ACs to contribute motion-sensitive excitatory input to ON DSGCs, ON-OFF DSGCs, and OFFα-RGCs without altering the diverse contrast preference of these targets.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the functional significance of the depth-dependent contrast preferences.

claim: When VG3-ACs were removed from the retina, inhibitory input to SbC-RGCs was reduced for OFF but not ON stimuli.
source: Nonetheless, when VG3-ACs were removed from the retina, inhibitory input to SbC-RGCs was reduced for OFF but not ON stimuli (Tien et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a finding from previous research supported by citation.

claim: The local processing of ON and OFF signals observed in VG3-AC arbors could help explain the selective deficit in inhibitory input to SbC-RGCs for OFF but not ON stimuli.
source: The local processing of ON and OFF signals we observe in VG3-AC arbors could help explain this selective deficit.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation connecting the current findings to previous observations.

claim: Population activity in the VG3-AC plexus reflects local presynaptic input patterns rather than postsynaptic identity.
source: Finally, we find that, because of local processing, population activity in the VG3-AC plexus reflects local presynaptic input patterns rather than postsynaptic identity and represents visual space in remarkably precise continuous topographic maps.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Population activity in the VG3-AC plexus represents visual space in remarkably precise continuous topographic maps.
source: Finally, we find that, because of local processing, population activity in the VG3-AC plexus reflects local presynaptic input patterns rather than postsynaptic identity and represents visual space in remarkably precise continuous topographic maps.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: VG3-Cre mice were crossed to the Ai9 tdTomato reporter strain to allow targeting of VG3-ACs under two-photon guidance for filling with Oregon Green BAPTA-1.
source: To allow targeting of VG3-ACs under two-photon guidance for filling with Oregon Green BAPTA-1, we crossed VG3-Cre mice to the Ai9 tdTomato reporter strain (Madisen et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the experimental approach.

claim: Mice were housed in a 12 hr light/dark cycle and fed ad libidum.
source: Mice were housed in a 12 hr light/dark cycle and fed ad libidum.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about animal husbandry.

claim: Retinas were isolated from mice of both sexes aged between postnatal day 30 (P30) and P45.
source: We isolated retinas from mice of both sexes aged between postnatal day 30 (P30) and P45.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the experimental subjects.

claim: All procedures in this study were approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee of Washington University School of Medicine (Protocol # 20170033).
source: All procedures in this study were approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee of Washington University School of Medicine (Protocol # 20170033) and were performed in compliance with the National Institutes of Health Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals.
evidence: This is a statement about ethical compliance.

claim: Optic nerve crush reduced the RGC density by 74%.
source: This revealed that optic nerve crush reduced the RGC density by 74%.
evidence: This is a finding from the optic nerve crush control experiment.

claim: Conditional probabilities for co-staining were P(VGluT3-positive | GCaMP6f-positive)=1 (n = 111 cells) and P(GCaMP6f-positive | VGluT3-positive)=0.98 (n = 113 cells).
source: Conditional probabilities for co-staining were P(VGluT3-positive | GCaMP6f-positive)=1 (n = 111 cells) and P(GCaMP6f-positive | VGluT3-positive)=0.98 (n = 113 cells).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the immunohistochemistry validation.

claim: Visual stimuli were written in MATLAB using the Cogent Graphics toolbox.
source: Visual stimuli were written in MATLAB (The Mathworks, Natick, MA) using the Cogent Graphics toolbox (John Romaya, Laboratory of Neurobiology at the Wellcome Department of Imaging Neuroscience, University College London, UK).
evidence: This is a methodological detail about stimulus generation.

claim: All stimuli were centered on the two-photon scan field and their average intensity was kept constant at ~1600 s-opsin isomerizations/S cone/s.
source: All stimuli were centered on the two-photon scan field and their average intensity was kept constant at ~1600 s-opsin isomerizations/S cone/s.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about stimulus presentation.

claim: A custom-built upright two-photon microscope controlled by the Scanimage r3.8 MATLAB toolbox was used in this study.
source: A custom-built upright two-photon microscope (Scientifica) controlled by the Scanimage r3.8 MATLAB toolbox was used in this study; and images were acquired via a DAQ NI PCI6110 data acquisition board (National Instruments, Austin, TX).
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the imaging setup.

claim: GCaMP6f and Oregon Green BAPTA-1 were excited with a Mai-Tai laser tuned to 940 nm.
source: GCaMP6f and Oregon Green BAPTA-1 were excited with a Mai-Tai laser (Spectra-Physics, Santa Clara, CA) tuned to 940 nm, and fluorescence emission was collected via a 60 × 1.0 NA water immersion objective (Olympus) filtered through consecutive 450 nm long-pass (Thorlabs, Newton, NJ) and 513–528 nm band-pass filters (Chroma, Bellows Falls, VT).
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the imaging setup.

claim: Image segmentation was more reliable at the higher pixel density.
source: Because image segmentation was more reliable at the higher pixel density and measurements of response transience were indistinguishable between both scan rates (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), we acquired images throughout this study at 9.5 Hz with a pixel density of 4.7 pixels / μm2.
evidence: This is a justification for the methodological choice of imaging parameters.

claim: Borders between IPL and adjacent layers were detected in transmitted light images.
source: Borders were detected in transmitted light images (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a methodological detail about depth registration.

claim: Scan fields at different IPL depths were imaged in pseudorandom order.
source: Scan fields at different IPL depths were imaged in pseudorandom order, and for each scan, the retina was allowed to adapt to the laser light for 30 s before presentation of visual stimuli.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about the imaging protocol.

claim: Throughout the experiments, retinas were perfused at ~7 mL/min with 34°C mACSFNaHCO3 equilibrated with 95% O2/5% CO2.
source: Throughout the experiments, retinas were perfused at ~7 mL/min with 34°C mACSFNaHCO3 equilibrated with 95% O2/5% CO2.
evidence: This is a methodological detail about tissue maintenance during experiments.

claim: A serial clustering procedure was developed to identify functional processing domains in VG3-AC neurites with minimal assumptions and user involvement.
source: To identify functional processing domains in VG3-AC neurites with minimal assumptions and user involvement, we developed a serial clustering procedure, in which a functional clustering algorithm is successively applied to different image features.
evidence: This is a methodological innovation described in the study.

claim: The functional clustering algorithm was based on Shekhar et al. (2016).
source: The functional clustering algorithm was based on Shekhar et al. (2016), beginning with principal components analysis to reduce the dimensionality of the input feature to the minimum needed to explain 80% of its variance.
evidence: This describes the basis of the analysis method with citation.

claim: A polarity index of 1 indicates pure ON responses, whereas a polarity index of −1 indicates pure OFF responses.
source: A polarity index of 1 indicates pure ON responses, whereas a polarity index of −1 indicates pure OFF responses.
evidence: This defines the polarity index metric used in the analysis.

claim: Response transience was weakly correlated with response amplitude (R2 = 0.0187, p<10−34, n = 3631 ROIs).
source: Because response transience was weakly correlated with response amplitude (R2 = 0.0187, p<10−34, n = 3631 ROIs), we corrected transience indices by linear regression and rejected responses to ON or OFF stimuli if their maximal amplitude was <25% of the OFF or ON responses of the same ROI, respectively.
evidence: This is a statistical finding that informed the analysis approach.

claim: Receptive field center size was defined as equivalent to the stimulus size eliciting the maximal response.
source: Consistent with previous studies (Crook et al., 2008), we defined receptive field center size as equivalent to the stimulus size eliciting the maximal response (Figure 2).
evidence: This defines the metric used for receptive field center size with citation to previous work.
